registeredBeforeResults: When this file was committed no A13 number of any kind existed: no close-to-open return had been computed for any list on any split, and tools/gapper-study/a13_overnight.py had not been written. Known at that moment and possibly related: the D-1 16:00 boosted AUC 0.899 and precision@10 0.163 for reach20By0945 (runs/explore/visibility-20261109-1604.md), the watchlist's recall of +100% runners (watchlist-20261109-1945.md), the repeat-runner rate (7.1% of +100% runners run +100% again within 5 sessions), 'buying gappers already up 20% at the open loses 5.2% by the close', and the auctions run's open-cross versus 09:30-bar-open comparison. None of these is an overnight return.
question: Does buying a small evening list at the D-1 daily close and selling at the D daily open net at least +1.0%/trade after costs? Every long rule tested so far bought after the move was visible and held intraday; the cited literature (Berkman et al. 2012; Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019) says attention stocks earn overnight and give back intraday. The close-to-open leg has never been tested here.

data.weights: none (whole universe, equal weight per trade)

trade.exit: D daily open, D = the symbol's next daily bar; a later next bar within 5 sessions exits at its open; none within 5 sessions = -100%

eligibilityAtS.splitExclusion: no split ex-date from S-25 calendar days through D

statedLookAhead: Signals use the complete S daily bar and the fill is that bar's close; a market-on-close order must be entered by about 15:50 ET. The leak favours the rule, so a fail is decisive and a pass requires the minute-level replication in decisionRules.

signals.S1: S volume >= 3 x 20-session average share volume; rank by S close / prior close - 1, descending
signals.S2: S1's volume rule AND S close / prior close - 1 >= 0.20 AND S close >= low + 0.75 x (high - low); rank as S1

costModel.name: A13-auction-conservative
costModel.roundTrip: max(classic Corwin-Schultz spread over the 20 sessions through S, 0.010) + 2 x TradingCosts.SquareRootImpact(shares = 1000 / S close, adv = 20-session average share volume, sigma = 20-session sigma, params impact constant)
costModel.whyNotA12: A12's multipliers scale the minute-bar Corwin-Schultz feature held only on candidate and sample days

hypotheses.claim: The train-selected configuration (highest day-clustered lower bound among those with >= 150 trades on >= 40 days) nets >= +1.0%/trade after the A13 cost.
hypotheses.method: Equal weight per trade on the four evaluation windows; day-clustered bootstrap (10,000 draws, seed 1337, 95%); SPA across the nine configurations; DSR at the ledger's trial count after the run.

hypotheses.claim: Descriptive: the share and mean of trades opening >= +10%, >= +20%, <= -10%, <= -20%, the same base rates over all eligible symbol-days, and top-1%/top-5% P&L concentration. No verdict.

decisionRules.onTrainFail: Stop. Validation is not read; no other signal, list size, exit or cost is tried under A13.
decisionRules.validation: Only after a train pass, noted in amendment-13.md first; read once, S3 fit on all of train, the selected configuration unchanged, the same minimums.
decisionRules.afterValidationPass: Minute-level replication (signals through 15:50 ET, closing-cross entry, opening-cross exit, quoted spreads for traded symbol-days) under its own amendment before anything else.
decisionRules.corrections: Own family F13; never enters the frozen A01-A12 corrections or Holm set.
decisionRules.promotion: Single holdout run only with the owner's explicit go-ahead, then 20 paper-shadow sessions; only the owner enables anything. This amendment never arms, sizes, places or exits an order.
